reviews.boundary_analysis: Example configuration and Development files remain secret-bearing surfaces; fake-value and UserSecretsId exclusions depend on actual sensitivity. The baseline explicitly includes these scope refinements and the development-contract exception to ignoring local files. Container/build-argument exposure is registered in RULE-K1-0369. No missing independent secret obligation found.

Leaf guidance narrows appsettings to structure/nonsecret defaults, makes Azure conditional on actual hosting, prefers workload/federated identity, and requires delivery verification including clean-environment independence. Each is separately represented at its conditional strength in the union. Snapshot/Monitor/named-options hypotheses are different RUN-022 questions, not new secret clauses.

The boundary enumerates external responses/messages as well as HTTP input. Command-argument separation, storage-boundary normalization, prohibition on arbitrary runtime-type deserialization, contextual resource limits and dedicated manual threat review all have independent prior claims. Existing uncertain labels do not erase that semantic coverage.

Raw SQL, micro-ORM and ADO.NET are within the prohibition; interpolation-parameterizing APIs and ordinary ORM predicates are expressly safe patterns. Both prohibition and scan false-positive exclusion are already registered, without requiring an SQL injection finding merely from input occurrence.

Client token attachment, route guards and filtering remain UX; resource-specific permissions use ASP.NET resource authorization or explicit Application logic. These alternatives and backend-verification requirement are represented; no requirement that every permission use one mechanism is inferred.

Explicit AllowAnonymous under authenticated-default policy, stable capability policy constants, avoidance of compound role strings, and evaluating effective global/fallback policy instead of demanding attributes are all recorded. Public access is checked for intent, not automatically reported vulnerable; probe topology exception also registered in EXTRA-K1-0173.

No-redirection permission requires both a secure deployed transport boundary and redirection not desired, explicitly captured by BF-0177 and primary. Certificate-validation prohibition remains absolute in prose; the local TrustServerCertificate example tension already exists as BF-0048, so it is not a fresh hypothesis.

Security-scan strengthens implementation guidance into never recommending custom cryptography and rejects blanket encryption/scanner-driven dependencies. Password hashing rather than reversible encryption, nonsecurity-checksum exclusion and purpose-specific data-at-rest mechanisms are expressly represented by the union, including contextual rather than automatic vulnerability judgments.

Public noncredentialed APIs may use unrestricted origins; credentialed origins must be restricted. Scan reviews actual exposure, not a universal wildcard prohibition. Development API-base-URL compatibility with backend CORS is an additional explicit setup condition already registered in EXTRA-K1-0221.
